title: n8n, Zapier, or Make — pick your stack
subtitle: Five honest questions, one opinionated recommendation. Built by someone who runs all three in production.

intro.paragraph: I've shipped automation in n8n, Zapier, and Make for the last four years. Most 'which tool' posts are written by people selling one of them. This one isn't — pick the wrong stack and you'll either pay 5x for what you need or fight self-hosting at 2am. Five questions, then I'll tell you what I'd actually build.

result_zapier.headline: Zapier — and don't apologize for it
result_zapier.body_html:
For your volume and team, Zapier is the right call. The hate Zapier gets online is mostly from engineers who could build it themselves; if you're a small team gluing SaaS apps under 1,000 runs/month, you'll ship 10x faster with Zapier than with Make or n8n.

Where Zapier earns its premium: the integration library is unmatched, the error UX is the best in the category, and your non-technical teammates can actually own workflows without you. Where it bites: pricing scales fast past 5,000 tasks/month, and complex branching gets ugly.

Start with the Professional plan ($73/mo at the time of writing), build 5-10 zaps, and revisit in 6 months. If you cross 5,000 tasks/month with growing complexity, that's your signal to migrate to Make or n8n.

result_make.headline: Make (Integromat) — best price-to-power ratio
result_make.body_html:
Make is the answer when you've outgrown Zapier's pricing but you're not ready for n8n's self-host overhead. It handles 80% of what n8n does for 30% of the operational burden.

It's the right call for branching logic, mid-volume work, and most AI-glue use cases. The visual editor is the best in the category once you adapt to the radial flow (give it 2 days, you'll prefer it).

Where Make wins: error handling is genuinely good, iteration through arrays is first-class, and the pricing is fair (~$30-50/mo for serious use). Where it loses: ecosystem is smaller than Zapier, and once you need custom self-hosted services or full code freedom, you'll hit a ceiling that n8n doesn't have.

For 90% of $1-10M service firms, Make + a couple of Lambdas / Cloud Functions is the actual right answer. Not n8n. Not Zapier.

alternatives.name: n8n

alternatives.name: Zapier
alternatives.when_to_consider: If your team is fully non-technical and you'd rather pay 3x for better UX and the deepest integration library.

result_n8n.headline: n8n — and probably self-hosted
result_n8n.body_html:
n8n is the right call. You've got either the volume, the custom-code needs, or the technical bench to justify it — and once you're in, you'll never go back.

What n8n unlocks: full JS in code nodes, native LangChain / AI agent support, your own Postgres for state, webhooks without rate limits, and the ability to fork the platform if you ever need to. The self-hosted edition runs on a $5/mo Railway box and handles tens of thousands of executions/day.

The catch is real: you own the uptime. Backups, version control, error monitoring — all on you. If your team can't handle a 2am alert when the queue worker dies, pay for n8n Cloud (~$50/mo) and let them deal with it.

This is what I run for my own business and almost every client. Start with the queue + worker mode from day 1, mirror your prod database, and keep workflows in git via the public API. You'll thank yourself in 12 months.

alternatives.name: Make
alternatives.when_to_consider: If you want 80% of n8n's power without owning a server. Real answer for most teams.

alternatives.name: Temporal / Inngest
alternatives.when_to_consider: If your workflows are truly bespoke long-running jobs (>1hr) and you have full-time engineers.
